data_points.claim: TikTok users are sticking bobby pins — and sometimes paperclips or forks — to the center of the forehead and watching them stay.
Dr Sara Webb, astrophysicist and Associate Dean at Swinburne, told news.com.au the effect is surface tension from natural skin oils (sebum).
data_points.source_name: Khaleej Times quoting news.com.au / Sara Webb

data_points.claim: The center of the forehead works better because it is flatter than the temples, so the pin can lie flat.
The trick is not magnetism or a 'third eye.' The brain's electromagnetic field is far too weak to hold metal.
Sebum plus skin micro-texture create enough adhesion/friction to balance a light, flat metal object.
Paramount and Legendary launched what they call the first playable full-length movie trailer on YouTube Playables (Street Fighter Combo Challenge) around Sep 1 2026.

misconceptions.myth: If it sticks, your third eye is open / you are psychic.
misconceptions.reality: A light flat object sticks on oily, relatively flat skin. Wellness captions are optional fanfic.

misconceptions.myth: The forehead is magnetically attracting metal.
misconceptions.reality: Brain EMF is orders of magnitude too weak. The bond is sebum + surface tension + friction.
misconceptions.source: Times Now; Sara Webb via Khaleej Times

misconceptions.myth: It only works on special people.
misconceptions.reality: Placement (flat center) and skin oil explain most of the variance.

research_summary: This week's stitchable TikTok/YouTube trend is a bobby pin that sticks to your forehead. Wellness captions call it a magnetic third eye. A Swinburne astrophysicist told Australian press it is sebum and surface tension, and the flat center of the forehead is why it works. That is the 30-second short.
